arxiv-2210-07649.title: Generic role of the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in nanocrystalline ferromagnets
arxiv-2210-07649.creator: Sergey Erokhin, Dmitry Berkov, Andreas Michels
arxiv-2210-07649.description: Abstract Motivated by recent experimental polarized neutron results, we present a numerical micromagnetic study of the interfacial (intergrain) Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) in nanocrystalline terbium. We demonstrate that the DMI-induced spin misalignment between adjacent nanograins is the reason for the formation of the asymmetric positive-negative pattern seen in polarized neutron scattering experiments.

arxiv-2302-11466.title: Advancements in Federated Learning: Models, Methods, and Privacy DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Journal: JACM CCS: Theory of computation Theory and algorithms for application domains CCS: Networks Network architectures CCS: Computing methodologies Distributed computing methodologies CCS: Security and privacy
arxiv-2302-11466.creator: Huiming Chen, Huandong Wang, Qingyue Long, Depeng Jin, Yong Li
arxiv-2302-11466.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Huiming Chen, Huandong Wang, Qingyue Long, Depeng Jin, Yong Li. Federated learning (FL) is a promising technique for resolving the rising privacy and security concerns. Its main ingredient is to cooperatively learn the model among the distributed clients without uploading any sensitive data. In this paper, we conducted a thorough review of the related works, following the development context and deeply mining the key technologies behind FL from the perspectives of theory and application.

arxiv-2503-06861.title: Enhanced Multi-Tuple Extraction for Alloys: Integrating Pointer Networks and Augmented Attention
arxiv-2503-06861.creator: Mengzhe Hei, Zhouran Zhang, Qingbao Liu, Yan Pan, Xiang Zhao, Yongqian Peng, Yicong Ye, Xin Zhang, Shuxin Bai
arxiv-2503-06861.description: Abstract Extracting high-quality structured information from scientific literature is crucial for advancing material design through data-driven methods. Despite the considerable research in natural language processing for dataset extraction, effective approaches for multi-tuple extraction in scientific literature remain scarce due to the complex interrelations of tuples and contextual ambiguities.

arxiv-2511-16124.title: VTinker: Guided Flow Upsampling and Texture Mapping for High-Resolution Video Frame Interpolation
arxiv-2511-16124.creator: Chenyang Wu, Jiayi Fu, Chun-Le Guo, Shuhao Han, Chongyi Li
arxiv-2511-16124.description: Abstract Due to large pixel movement and high computational cost, estimating the motion of high-resolution frames is challenging. Thus, most flow-based Video Frame Interpolation (VFI) methods first predict bidirectional flows at low resolution and then use high-magnification upsampling (e.g., bilinear) to obtain the high-resolution ones. However, this kind of upsampling strategy may cause blur or mosaic at the flows’ edges.

pmc-11484198.creator: Hussein N. Ghanem, Asmaa A. El-Zaher, Sally T. Mahmoud, Enas A. Taha
pmc-11484198.description: Novel univariate and chemometrics-aided UV spectrophotometric methods were tailored to undergo the fundamentals of green and white analytical chemistry for the simultaneous estimation of a ternary mixture of olanzapine (OLA), fluoxetine HCL (FLU), and its toxic impurity 4-(Trifluoromethyl) phenol (FMP) without any prior separation.

pmc-11634407.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Screening Tests for Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy: An Umbrella Review
pmc-11634407.creator: María Mogilevskaya, Mariana Gaviria-Carrillo, John Edwin Feliciano-Alfonso, Ana M. Barragan, Carlos A. Calderon-Ospina, Mauricio O. Nava-Mesa
pmc-11634407.description: Peripheral neuropathy is a common cause of morbidity in diabetes. Despite recent advancements in early diagnosis methods, there is a need for practical, highly sensitive, and cost-effective screening methods in clinical practice. This study summarizes evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses on the diagnostic accuracy of validated screening methods for diabetic peripheral neuropathy.

pmc-12450866.title: Gut microbiota profile in adults with abdominal obesity and non-abdominal obesity: links to body composition and macronutrient intake in Semarang, Indonesia—a brief research report
pmc-12450866.creator: Farhan Syafiq Fadhillah, Fariz Budi Arafat, Nani Maharani, Jihan Fadhilah, Hainun Zariyah, Mochamad Ali Sobirin, Hiroyuki Tsutsui, Adi Wibowo, Achmad Zulfa Juniarto, Adriyan Pramono
pmc-12450866.description: BackgroundAbdominal obesity is a significant risk factor for metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular diseases, with increasing evidence highlighting the role of gut microbiota in its development. In Indonesia, where 23.4% of adults are obese, few studies have examined the gut microbiota in relation to abdominal obesity, particularly in the context of unique dietary patterns.

pmc-12613371.title: Putative promiscuous symbionts in deep-sea corals and crinoids may contribute to nitrogen cycling
pmc-12613371.creator: Flúvio Modolon, Alessandro N Garritano, Lilian J Hill, Gustavo Duarte, Amanda Bendia, Rafael de Moura, Vivian Pellizari, Torsten Thomas, Raquel S Peixoto
pmc-12613371.description: BackgroundCrinoids (feather stars) are frequently found in association with corals, yet the physiological and microbial interactions between these organisms remain poorly understood. Both corals and crinoids host symbiotic microorganisms, but the functional roles of these symbionts, particularly in deep-sea environments, are largely unexplored.

pmc-12678130.title: Enteropathy-associated t-cell lymphoma presenting as refractory cutaneous ulcers in a 28-year-old male: a case report and literature review
pmc-12678130.creator: Dejie Zhao, Quanlin Li, Dan Liu, Jie Xu, Zheng Liu, Yanan Zhao, Zhixin Cheng, Ming Liu
pmc-12678130.description: BackgroundEnteropathy associated T-cell lymphoma (EATL) is a rare and aggressive subtype of peripheral T-cell lymphoma, most commonly associated with celiac disease (CD). It typically presents with gastrointestinal symptoms and carries a poor prognosis. Cutaneous involvement as the initial manifestation, particularly in the form of refractory skin ulcers in young patients, is rare.

pmc-12840294.title: A Multi-Branch Training Strategy for Enhancing Neighborhood Signals in GNNs for Community Detection
pmc-12840294.creator: Yuning Guo, Qiang Wu, Linyuan Lü
pmc-12840294.description: The tasks of community detection in complex networks have garnered increasing attention from researchers. Concurrently, with the emergence of graph neural networks (GNNs), these models have rapidly become the mainstream approach for solving this task. However, GNNs frequently encounter the Laplacian oversmoothing problem, which dilutes the crucial neighborhood signals essential for community identification.

pmc-13225155.title: Impact of static and dynamic magneto-mechanical stimulation with vortex microdiscs on glioblastoma cells cultured on 2D substrates with physiological stiffness
pmc-13225155.creator: Andrea Visonà, Sébastien Soulan, Bernard Dieny, Robert Morel, Alice Nicolas
pmc-13225155.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). External mechanical stresses acting on cellular compartments critically regulate cell behaviour and can induce cell death. Magnetically actuated particles present a promising strategy to apply such forces in a controlled manner, with potential applications in cancer therapy. In this study, we investigate the effects of actuating vortex magnetic microdiscs on a glioblastoma cell line cultured on soft, biomimetic substrates that mimic in vivo stiffness.

pmc-13558877.title: Nanoliposomal curcumin as a potential pro-apoptotic agent for cervical cancer: Evidence from Bcl-2 and Bax modulation in HeLa cells
pmc-13558877.creator: Subandi Subandi, Oktalia N. Aisyah, Bayu Lestari
pmc-13558877.description: Cervical cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, and treatment effectiveness is often limited by drug resistance and systemic toxicity. Curcumin has shown anticancer activity, but its clinical translation is constrained by poor solubility and low bioavailability. Nanoliposomal curcumin (Cur-NLPs) may improve intracellular delivery; however, its dose-dependent effect on apoptosis-related proteins in cervical cancer cells remains insufficiently defined.

pmc-13677718.title: Structure based discovery of antipsychotic-like TAAR1 agonists
pmc-13677718.creator: Sijie Huang, Heng Liu, Yujin Wu, Joao M Braz, Divya Kranthi, Brendan W Hall, Xinyue Zhang, Dmytro S Radchenko, Yurii S Moroz, John J Irwin, Allan I Basbaum, H Eric Xu, William C Wetsel, Brian K Shoichet
pmc-13677718.description: Schizophrenia is a severe mental illness whose current treatments primarily target dopamine and serotonin receptors. These drugs often cause side effects and vary in effectiveness across patients. The trace amine-associated receptor 1 (TAAR1), which modulates monoamine signaling, has emerged as a promising alternative target.
